I don't have any notes on Psalm 85 to give you yet. My research tools stopped working before I could open a single page. The first time I tried to fetch the planned sources, I got "no more code_execution tool calls remaining," so no web pages were retrieved.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and leave out anything I couldn't find. So I haven't written any notes. Anything I wrote now would come from memory without a source, which is exactly what you asked me not to do.

**Pages I was going to read first:**
- Enduring Word (David Guzik): enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-85/
- Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary: biblehub.com/commentaries/[gill|ellicott|pulpit]/psalms/85.htm
- Precept Austin: preceptaustin.org/psalm-85-commentary
- NET Bible translators' notes: netbible.org/bible/Psalms+85
- Augustine on this psalm: newadvent.org/fathers/1801085.htm (in the Latin Bible's numbering it's Psalm 84)

**What I'd add next:**
- Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (spurgeon.org or ccel.org)
- Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu)
- Calvin's commentary (ccel.org)
- Lutheran and Orthodox material (lcms.org, 1517.org, oca.org)

These might bring up points where the traditions differ, especially on v. 10 ("righteousness and peace have kissed"). Many writers apply that verse to Christ and the cross, so it's a likely place for different readings to show up.

If you ask again in a new message, the tools should be available and I can do the full sourced write-up.
